study: Pilot 0 A2-0: structural audit of transition observables
scope: Semantic and logical contract only. No new model generation, no latent-factor inference, no predictor search, and no update to B, C, H1, or CARS.

terminology.reserved_for: success under the verified-error intervention within the relevant frozen interface

population_boundary: All transition quantities are defined only on initially-wrong frozen prestates, matching the historical eligible populations.

T_change.definition: neutral revision count divided by two neutral branches
T_change.identified_property: propensity to leave the realized wrong answer under neutral review

Q_N.definition: neutral branches ending correct divided by neutral branches that revised; undefined when no neutral branch revised
Q_N.identified_property: quality of a neutral transition conditional on revision

T_instability.definition: 1 iff the two neutral-review branches end on different option letters, else 0
T_instability.identified_property: replicate-level transition instability under neutral review

T_verified.definition: verified-error branches ending correct divided by two verified-error branches
T_verified.identified_property: evidence-conditioned correction success under the relevant verified-error interface

G_verified_minus_neutral.definition: T_verified - C2_neutral_self_correction_rate within the same frozen-prestate block
G_verified_minus_neutral.label: verified-minus-neutral correction-success contrast
G_verified_minus_neutral.authority: Within a randomized historical interface this contrasts final correctness under verified-error versus neutral-review branches. It is not an interface-invariant scalar called evidence responsiveness.

logical_dependencies: For an initially-wrong prestate, every neutral self-correction is necessarily a revision.
At the branch level: neutral_correct => neutral_revised.
At the block-rate level: C2_neutral_self_correction <= T_change.
High T_change does not imply high Q_N.
High T_instability does not imply beneficial or harmful transition quality.
Low T_change does not imply poor epistemic adaptation.
High T_verified does not imply high neutral revisability.
A state property does not imply a transition property; a transition property does not imply transition quality.
prohibited_representations: Treat C1, C2, C3, and C4 as exchangeable indicators in a factor analysis.
Count C1 and C2 as independent evidence for dimensionality despite their logical nesting.
Interpret revision frequency as correction capacity without transition-quality evidence.
Interpret instability normatively without an external quality criterion.
Interpret G_verified_minus_neutral as interface-invariant evidence responsiveness.
Introduce S2, S3, a composite confidence score, or a new moderator during A2.
Create A1-V or expand B1 sensitivity during A2.
A2_D_question: What empirical transition topology is supported by T_change, Q_N, T_instability, and T_verified across the existing historical interface strata?

representation_hypotheses.H_T1_COMMON: The distinct transition dimensions exhibit sufficiently coherent replicated ordering that a common target representation remains plausible.
representation_hypotheses.H_T2_SEPARABLE: At least several distinct transition dimensions are empirically weakly coupled enough that collapsing them to one ordering would lose substantive information.
representation_hypotheses.H_T3_INTERFACE_CONDITIONED: The transition profile differs between interface families beyond the variation observed across the two legacy-interface replications.

non_exclusivity: H_T1, H_T2, and H_T3 are representation signals, not mutually exclusive exhaustive truths. A2-D may return mixed structure or unresolved structure.
authority_boundary: A2-0 contains no empirical topology result.
A2-D will be historical discovery, not prospective construct validation.
No A2 result by itself licenses a latent trait, new moderator, B/C update, H1 update, or CARS revision.
